title: Help and current features
text: Josi CE provides one self-hosted workspace with conversations, tasks, approvals, contacts, memory, model providers, connected accounts, operational mail, documents, external messaging channels, backups, diagnostics, an installable web app, optional Voice Box, and integrations. Administrators configure the installation under Admin . Members use their own accounts under Workspace .

title: First-run recovery key
text: The setup wizard shows the recovery key once. Select Copy key or Download key , store it away from the Josi computer, and then confirm that it was saved. There is no separate terminal command for this step.

title: Backups and system checkup
text: Admin → Overview shows installation status and recommendations. Admin → System checkup runs Josi Doctor. It explains problems, offers only bounded automatic repairs, asks for approval, and verifies the result. It also checks the stable release channel and applies an exactly approved update only after creating a backup. Admin → Backups creates backups and configures SMB or NFS storage. Keep the recovery key separately from the backup destination.

title: Integrations
text: Admin → Integrations connects model providers and external services. Credentials stay in the Master Vault. Consequential writes and deletes still require approval.

title: Family / Parental Controls BETA
text: Do not rely on these controls for a child's safety. They control only access to Josi. They do not lock a device, block other apps or websites, monitor location or actual screen time, contact emergency services, or replace active adult supervision and proven device-level controls.

title: 1. Run the installer
text: Install and open Docker first. You do not need Git, Node.js, a source checkout, or a Josi command-line tool. Choose the command for your computer and paste the whole block into Terminal.

title: Mac
text: mkdir -p "$HOME/josi-ce" && cd "$HOME/josi-ce" && \ docker run --rm \ -p 8080:8080 \ -v "$HOME/.docker/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock" \ -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" \ docker.io/romanvaxman/josi-ce-installer:latest

title: Linux
text: mkdir -p "$HOME/josi-ce" && cd "$HOME/josi-ce" && \ docker run --rm \ -p 8080:8080 \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" \ docker.io/romanvaxman/josi-ce-installer:latest The installer prints a private setup URL and a one-time setup code. Leave the Terminal window open while setup is running. The temporary installer can control Docker so it can create the Josi services. It exits when installation finishes. Normal Josi services do not receive the Docker socket.

title: 2. Finish setup in your browser
text: Open the setup URL printed in Terminal. Accept the temporary local-certificate warning. Enter the one-time setup code. Choose whether Josi is available on this computer, your local network, a public domain, or through an existing proxy or tunnel. Optionally choose one project folder for coding features. Skip it if you do not need Josi to work with local files. Review the choices and select Install Josi . The browser installer writes the configuration, generates the installation secrets, downloads the published images, starts Josi, and checks that it opens.

title: 3. Open Josi
text: When installation succeeds, select Open Josi . The first person through setup becomes the administrator. Josi walks through the account, AI provider, privacy choices, and optional connections. When the recovery key appears, copy or download it and store it somewhere other than the Josi computer.

title: 4. Confirm it works
text: Open the Josi URL and send a message. If Josi opens and answers using the provider configured during setup, the installation works. You do not need to inspect containers or call health endpoints.

title: After installation
text: Use Josi's Admin screens for normal management: Overview shows status and recommendations. System checkup explains problems, offers safe automatic repairs, and installs approved stable updates. Network & address changes local, LAN, domain, proxy, or tunnel access. Backups creates backups and configures storage. Integrations connects providers and services. Users manages workspace access. Keep Docker running. On a dedicated Mac mini, enable Docker Desktop at login so Josi returns after a restart.

title: Use Josi on your devices
text: Your Josi server is the home for every client. The web app and native apps use the same account, workspace, conversations, memory, and tools. Android: Install Josi CE from Google Play . iPhone and iPad: The App Store release is coming soon. macOS, Windows, and Linux: Desktop downloads are in final device testing. Links will appear here when each build is approved. To connect a native app: Open Josi CE. Choose Public URL or Tailscale . Paste the Josi URL shown during server setup. Select Verify and continue . Sign in with the same Josi account you created in the browser. The app connects to the Josi server you just installed. It does not install or create another server.

title: Updating Josi
text: Open Admin → System checkup as a super-admin, select Check for updates , review the release notes, enter the exact confirmation shown, and approve the update. Josi creates a backup, applies the pinned release, verifies health, and rolls back automatically when a safe rollback is possible. If Josi cannot open or the maintenance helper is unavailable, run the same installer command again. The browser installer detects the existing installation and preserves its configuration and data. Do not delete the josi-ce folder or Docker volumes during an update.

title: Backups
text: Open Admin → Backups to create a backup or configure SMB/NFS storage. Keep the recovery key separately from the backup destination. A backup and the key protect different things, so you need both.

title: Docker is not running
text: Open Docker Desktop on Mac, or start Docker Engine on Linux, then run the same installer command again.

title: The Mac reports that the Docker socket does not exist
text: Wait until Docker Desktop says the engine is running, then retry. Josi uses Docker Desktop's user socket at $HOME/.docker/run/docker.sock .

title: Port 8080 is already in use
text: Stop the program using port 8080, then run the installer again. That port is used only for the temporary setup page.

title: The browser warns that the setup page is not private
text: This is expected for the temporary local setup certificate. Confirm that the address matches the one printed by the installer before continuing.

title: Setup was interrupted
text: Run the same installer command again. It reuses the $HOME/josi-ce directory and preserves completed configuration.

title: Josi installed but does not open
text: Return to the installer window and use its reported error. If Josi previously worked, open Admin → Overview for the system checkup. Do not delete Docker volumes or the installation directory while troubleshooting.

title: Privacy Notice
text: Effective 14 September 2026. Josi CE is self-hosted. The person or organization operating an installation is normally the controller of its data. SOCAL RECEPTIONIST LLC does not receive installation data merely because the software is running.

title: Data categories and purposes
text: Depending on enabled features, Josi processes account/authentication data; profiles and personalization; conversations, tasks, approvals and memory; contacts, calendars, email and connected-account identifiers; files, extracted text, indexes and citations; encrypted provider credentials; usage/cost records; audit events; backups; channel identifiers and messages; diagnostics/support material; and Voice Box audio. It uses these to authenticate, provide requested functions, enforce policy, connect services, operate and secure the installation, calculate configured limits, and back up or restore data.

title: Family BETA data
text: Family BETA processes the parent-child relationship, controls, schedules, distinct minutes in which a child sends a message, parental access events, and child conversations opened by the linked adult. It is not device or screen-time monitoring. Ending a relationship removes schedules, controls and activity-minute records; ordinary conversation retention remains controlled by the installation.

title: Who receives data
text: Data stays on the installation unless a user or operator enables or uses a destination. Necessary data may then go to the selected AI provider; Google or Microsoft; configured SMTP/mail services; Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp or Signal; configured storage/backup providers; configured GitHub, Netlify, Vercel, Supabase or other developer services; an operator-selected telemetry or support gateway; recipients and shared users authorized by the user; and public documentation/Groq only when optional help chat is enabled and used. Voice Box is intended to run locally. Disclosures may also occur when required by law, needed for safety/security, or in a lawful business transfer. SOCAL RECEPTIONIST LLC does not sell installation data, use it for advertising, or use private content to train generalized AI models. External providers operate under their own policies and may process data internationally.

title: Telemetry, support, retention and rights
text: Telemetry is off by default and excludes prompts, message content, contacts, calendars, credentials and identifiable business data. Support bundles are made locally for review and are not sent until approved to a configured gateway. Retention and deletion are controlled by the operator and feature settings; third-party and backup copies may follow separate retention. Contact the operator for access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection or portability. Privacy questions follow the repository's public Support and Security policies.

title: Children and security
text: The operator and supervising adult must obtain required consent, provide age-appropriate notice and comply with child-privacy law. Josi uses access controls, encrypted stored credentials, audit events, CSRF protection and a restrictive browser policy, but no system is perfectly secure and a host operator can bypass application controls.

title: Cookie Notice
text: Effective 14 September 2026. The official application uses only strictly necessary first-party cookies: an HTTP-only authentication session cookie (optionally persistent when “Keep me signed in” is selected) and a CSRF cookie paired with a request header. They are not used for advertising, cross-site tracking or analytics. The Content Security Policy prevents third-party scripts and resources from loading. The PWA caches versioned application files and an offline page, not private API responses or user content. Connected providers may set their own cookies on their sites during OAuth or sign-in. Signing out ends the server session; browser settings can clear cookies and the PWA cache. Operators are responsible for disclosing cookies introduced by modified builds.
